in_text_mentions: Another frequent problem is that a markedly distended stomach can displace the pylorus dorsally making it very difficult to access (Fig. 4). panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 5 panels (A, B, C, D, E). A: Erect plain abdominal radiograph on day 5 of life in this IHPS case report showing an enlarged stomach with an air-fluid level, consistent with gastric outlet obstruction from the pyloric stenosis; the distal bowel gas was described as unsuspicious, so no specific radiographic sign (string sign, paucity of distal gas, etc.) is claimed. The gastric enlargement is a captioned manifestation specific to this patient, so the panel is included with the nonspecific finding placed in proposed_findings. panels.figure_caption: (A–E): (A) Erect plain abdominal X-ray on day 5 of life showed an enlarged stomach with an air-fluid level but was otherwise unsuspicious. (B–E) Sonographic examination on the same day showed a failure to pass gastric content, illustrated here in a sequence of ultrasound images during the gastric peristaltic wave. Furthermore, shouldering of the pylorus can be seen pointed out by red markings in (E).
in_text_mentions: On the fifth day of life, a plain abdominal X-ray showed an enlarged stomach with an air-fluid level and an unsuspicious air distribution in the small bowel loops (Figure 1A). Ultrasound examination performed on the same day confirmed the finding of the enlarged stomach and added the information of functional gastric outlet obstruction because at no time during the examination an opening of the pylorus could be seen (Figure 1B–E). The thickness of the pyloric muscle was 3 mm, and the length of the pylorus was 1.3 cm.

panels.rationale: Genuine abdominal radiograph of a human infant (day 3 of life) with persistent nonbilious emesis, from a case report titled 'An Unusual Presentation of Neonatal Pyloric Stenosis.' The image shows a prominent gastric gas bubble/dilated stomach (orange arrow) and paucity of distal bowel gas (blue arrow), a plain-film pattern consistent with gastric outlet obstruction from hypertrophic pyloric stenosis. The distal bowel gas paucity maps directly to the configured radiology_xray vocabulary finding; the prominent gastric gas bubble is clearly present but absent from the vocabulary and is therefore proposed. No skin is shown; ethnicity and staging are not applicable. Classified as variant because neonatal presentation with plain-film diagnosis is a recognized less common form rather than the usual ultrasound-confirmed 2-6 week presentation.
